prerequisites: It is recommended that students have studied Chemistry in high school, which would provide knowledge of chemical formulation, the concept of a mole, different ways of expressing solution concentration, and stoichiometric calculations.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry, and their applications in engineering.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 1. FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS AND LAWS OF CHEMISTRY: Concept of Science. Object, importance, and classification of Chemistry. Classification of matter. Fundamental laws of chemical transformations. Dalton's atomic theory. Symbols and formulas. Formulation and nomenclature of chemical compounds. Concept of mole, Avogadro's number, molar volume. Determination of empirical and molecular formulas. Stoichiometric calculations.

UNIT 2. ATOMIC STRUCTURE: ATOMIC NUCLEUS: Elementary particles: the electron, the proton, and the neutron. Rutherford's atomic model. Atomic number and mass number. Isotopes and Isobars. Nuclear stability. Natural radioactivity. Kinetics of radioactive decay.

UNIT 3. ATOMIC STRUCTURE: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE: Matter-energy interaction. Atomic spectra. Bohr's atomic model. Extranuclear structure of the atom according to wave mechanics: wave-particle duality. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. Schrödinger equation for the hydrogen atom. Quantum numbers. Atomic orbitals.

UNIT 4. PERIODIC SYSTEM. PERIODIC LAW: Classification of elements: periodic law and periodic system. The atomic nucleus and the periodic table. Electrons and the periodic table: quantum mechanical explanation. Periodic variation of some physical and chemical atomic properties.
UNIT 5. CHEMICAL BONDING: Ionic bonding: Crystal lattices, lattice energy. Covalent bonding: Nature, Lewis structures and octet rule, molecular geometry and dipole moment. Bond order and bond length.

UNIT 6. INTERMOLECULAR FORCES. STATES OF MATTER. CHANGES OF STATE: Gaseous state: ideal gas laws, real gases, kinetic-molecular theory of gases. Liquid state: Properties. Solid state: Properties. Changes of state: phase diagram.

UNIT 7. DISPERSED SYSTEMS. SOLUTIONS. COLLIGATIVE PROPERTIES OF SOLUTIONS: Dispersed systems: classification. Solutions: solubility, ideal and non-ideal solutions, Raoult's law, Henry's law. Colligative properties of solutions containing non-volatile solutes.

UNIT 8. CHEMICAL REACTIONS: CHEMICAL THERMODYNAMICS: Basic terms in Thermodynamics. Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics. Heat. Work. First Law of Thermodynamics: Internal energy. Thermochemistry: Enthalpy, fundamental laws of Thermochemistry. Second Law of Thermodynamics: Entropy. Reversibility, spontaneity, and chemical equilibrium: Gibbs free energy.
UNIT 9. CHEMICAL REACTIONS: CHEMICAL KINETICS: Reaction rate. Elementary reactions. Reaction mechanism. General reaction rate equation: Reaction order. Theories of reaction rate. Catalysis.

UNIT 10. CHEMICAL EQUILIBRIUM: Expression of the equilibrium constant. Relationships between equilibrium constants. Relationship between chemical kinetics and chemical equilibrium. Modification of equilibrium conditions: Le Châtelier's principle. Equilibria in homogeneous and heterogeneous systems.

UNIT 11. ELECTROCHEMISTRY: Oxidation-reduction reactions. Electrochemical cells. Standard electrode potential. Thermodynamics of redox reactions. Nernst equation. Commercial voltaic cells. Corrosion. Electrolysis. Commercial electrolytic processes.
PRACTICE 2: ACID-BASE VOLUMETRIES: DETERMINATION OF VINEGAR ACIDITY.
PRACTICE 3: CHEMICAL KINETICS: ACID HYDROLYSIS OF METHYL ACETATE.
SEMINAR: WAYS OF EXPRESSING CONCENTRATION. CALCULATIONS IN THE CHEMISTRY LABORATORY.
PRACTICE 4: DISTILLATION OF AN ETHANOL-WATER MIXTURE
teaching_methods: Practical group classes (problems and lab sessions)

assessment_methods.method: Quizzes/questionnaires throughout the course (theory and problems)
Quizzes/questionnaires on in-class and seminar activities (formulation and nomenclature)

assessment_rules: According to the University of Jaén's Academic and Evaluation Regulations, evaluation is global, and each evaluated part must be passed to contribute to the final grade. The theoretical exam and quizzes count for 70%, the practical knowledge exam for 20%, and in-class/seminar activity quizzes for 10%. Grades from practical and in-class activities (20% and 10%) are retained for both ordinary and extraordinary exam periods. Students must attend practical sessions to take the practical exam.
